newsitem.title: ROMANIA: Romania reserve money rises 12.2 pct in December.
newsitem.headline: Romania reserve money rises 12.2 pct in December.

text.p: The daily average of Romania's reserve money, deemed the main instrument of central bank (BNR) monetary policy this year, was 7.1 trillion lei in December, 12.2 percent up on the previous month, BNR data showed.
Reserve money, also known as high-powered money, includes cash in circulation and in vaults and banks' minimum reserves.
"The rise in reserve money was a result of high demand for currency outside banks during winter holidays and an increase in banks' reserves," a BNR report showed on Friday.
Currency outside banks saw a 10.9 percent rise in December, when they took 73.4 percent of reserve money.
Banks' reserves climbed to 1.59 trillion lei in December from 1.4 trillion in November, reflecting excess liquidity in the banking system, the BNR said.
Central bank governor Mugur Isarescu said on Thursday his bank aimed to watch money supply expansion this year through tough control over reserve money, which he called "the core of broad money".
Romania is using monetary levers to fight rising inflation, restore confidence in the leu, which has sagged by 120 percent from 4,000 to the dollar earlier this year.

The BNR has started to mop up extra liquidity to create "leu hunger", pushing short-term rates to some 250 percent on Friday against 52 percent in early January on the back of a cash-starving money market.

Monthly inflation soared to 13.7 percent in January from 10.3 percent last December. A surge of price rises is expected in the months ahead following the freeing of prices for fuel, electicity and food, introduced this week. But it is forecast to slow to about 2.2 percent by end-1997.
